page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, consistently register in the weak to poor categories, reflecting the older CPU architecture. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 25.29 GB/sec and write speeds of 21.61 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks also demonstrate lower throughput, with gzip compression single-threaded performance at 19.01 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, this instance is suited for moderate, non-latency-sensitive workloads. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, development environments, small database operations, and lightweight Redis caching. The absence of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators limits its utility for high-performance computing, large-scale data processing, or machine learning workloads.
